## Outcome

Several branches were failing in CI, but the failures only looked related from the outside.

One came from an earlier renderer test leaving the shared Chromote timeout at one second. Another involved GitHub Pages tests running without the required organization token. A third came from the `atime` workflow loading the wrong package version while building an older baseline.

## What I Did

- Removed the leaked one-second Chromote timeout in [PR #337](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/337); the fix merged June 12.
- Opened [PR #338](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/338) to investigate GitHub Pages tests on forked pull requests without the organization token.
- Traced the `atime` failure to the workflow loading current Animint2 while testing an older baseline and opened [PR #341](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/341).
- Opened [PR #339](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/339) with a failing multiline strip test, then rendered each line as an SVG `<tspan>`.

## Learnings

I first treated the red CI jobs as one reliability problem. Tracing them separately showed that shared browser state, missing credentials, and package installation order needed different fixes.

## Challenges / Notes

Finding the cause did not yet tell me where each fix belonged. That decision continued into the next few weeks.

## Next Week Targets

Check which proposals belong in Animint2, which should be simplified, and which should move elsewhere.
